title: Everton hopeful of appointing Norwich’s Dean Rastrick as new academy director
content:
Everton are hopeful of appointing Norwich City’s head of football development Dean Rastrick as their new academy director.

Rastrick, formerly of Tottenham Hotspur, has emerged as the leading contender to fill the vacant post after an extensive search process led by technical director Nick Cox.

Talks have already taken place over the move, which would see Rastrick replace former academy director Gareth Prosser, who left for Al Jazira of the United Arab Emirates at the end of last season.

Head of academy coaching Carl Darlington took on the role on an interim basis while Prosser’s successor was found, but is now likely to return to his former duties. Darlington also played a key role behind the scenes in sourcing loan moves for the Everton’s young players, another position still to be filled by the club.

Should the move be confirmed as expected, Rastrick would oversee the process for a new loans manager and head of academy recruitment. James Vaughan, the former Everton striker, held both positions before leaving to join a sports management agency towards the end of last season.

Rastrick is well regarded in the game after his stints at Tottenham and Norwich. He began his career as a youth development officer at Luton Town before holding a similar position at Derby County. He joined Spurs in 2010 after four years with Norwich and spent 13 years in north London, working his way up from academy performance manager to academy manager.

During that 13-year stint, Rastrick played a role in the development of players like Mikey Moore, Troy Parrott, Oliver Skipp and Dane Scarlett.

“During his tenure with us, Dean has overseen the development of a large number of players who have progressed to enjoy careers in the Premier League, European football and the wider professional game,” Spurs said in a 2023 statement confirming his return to Norwich.

“He has also overseen a large number of individual success stories and tournament victories at home and abroad throughout the age groups, culminating in the recent Under-18 and Under-17 Premier League Cup successes. Dean has provided the academy with a clear strategy, leadership and vision to ensure we operate at the forefront of youth development.”

Rastrick also had a spell at the Professional Game Academy Audit Company (PGAAC) as leadership and management auditor.

He is now likely to work alongside technical director Cox, himself a former academy director, to reshape Everton’s youth programme.
